beats.title: Persia Conquers Egypt
beats.description: A Persian army beat the last native pharaoh's forces at Pelusium and made the Nile kingdom a province of a foreign empire.

beats.title: Alexander Enters Egypt
beats.description: The Macedonian king marched into the Nile valley without a fight and was welcomed as liberator, founding a new city on the coast.

beats.title: Caesar Arrives in Alexandria
beats.description: A Roman general chasing his rival landed in Egypt, took sides in a royal feud and was besieged in the palace quarter.

beats.title: Rome Annexes Egypt
beats.description: After the defeat of Antony and Cleopatra, Octavian took over the richest kingdom of the Mediterranean as a personal possession.

beats.title: Vandals Seize Carthage
beats.description: A Germanic people who had crossed from Spain captured the great North African port and set up their own kingdom there.

beats.title: Belisarius Invades Vandal Africa
beats.description: An eastern Roman fleet landed a small army near Carthage and soon toppled the Vandal kingdom to restore imperial rule.

beats.title: Arab Armies Invade Egypt
beats.description: A small force of Arab horsemen crossed from Palestine into the Nile delta, beginning the end of imperial rule from Constantinople.

beats.title: A French King Dies at Tunis
beats.description: A crusade led by the king of France landed near Carthage, but plague struck the camp and the king himself died.

beats.title: Portugal Captures Ceuta
beats.description: A Portuguese fleet stormed a Moroccan trading port across the strait, opening Europe's long push down the African coast.

beats.title: Sailors Pass Cape Bojador
beats.description: A Portuguese captain finally rounded the dreaded headland that mariners believed marked the edge of the navigable sea.

beats.title: Dias Rounds the Cape
beats.description: A Portuguese captain driven by storms sailed around the southern tip of the continent and proved the way to the Indian Ocean.

beats.title: Da Gama Sails Round Africa
beats.description: A Portuguese fleet rounded the southern cape and pushed up the east coast on the way to India, calling at Mozambique and Mombasa.
beats.note: Left Lisbon 1497; reached East African ports in 1498.

beats.title: Ottomans Conquer Egypt
beats.description: The sultan's army defeated the Mamluk rulers in Cairo and added the Nile valley to a vast Turkish empire.

beats.title: Charles V Takes Tunis
beats.description: A Habsburg emperor led a great fleet across the sea and drove a corsair admiral from the North African city.

beats.title: Portuguese Soldiers Reach Ethiopia
beats.description: A few hundred musketeers landed on the Red Sea coast to help the Christian emperor fight an invading sultanate's army.

beats.title: Portugal's King Dies in Morocco
beats.description: A young Portuguese king invaded Morocco with a crusading army and was killed as it was wiped out, ending his dynasty.

beats.title: Bruce Finds the Blue Nile's Source
beats.description: A Scottish traveller reached the spring in the Ethiopian highlands that he declared the headwaters of the Nile.

beats.title: African Association Founded
beats.description: A London dining club of gentlemen set out to fund explorers to find the Niger and the fabled city of Timbuktu.
beats.why_in: founded to send expeditions to Africa

beats.title: Mungo Park Reaches the Niger
beats.description: A young Scottish surgeon saw the great river flowing eastward, settling a long European debate about its direction.

beats.title: Napoleon Invades Egypt
beats.description: A French army landed at Alexandria and won at the Pyramids, bringing scholars as well as soldiers to the Nile.

beats.title: Fleet Bombards Algiers
beats.description: A British and Dutch squadron pounded the corsair stronghold's harbour until its ruler freed Christian captives.
beats.why_in: European naval attack in North Africa

beats.title: France Invades Algiers
beats.description: A French expeditionary force landed west of the city and captured it, beginning a conquest that would last decades.

beats.title: Boers Win at Blood River
beats.description: Trekking Afrikaner farmers with wagons and guns defeated a vast Zulu army beside a river in Natal.

beats.title: Livingstone Arrives in Africa
beats.description: A young Scottish missionary and doctor landed at the Cape, starting the career that would carry him across the continent.

beats.title: Abd el-Kader Surrenders
beats.description: The emir who had led Algerian resistance to the French invaders for fifteen years laid down his arms and was exiled.

beats.title: Barth Sets Out Across the Sahara
beats.description: A German scholar joined a British expedition from Tripoli and spent years mapping the Sahel and its cities.

beats.title: Livingstone Sees Victoria Falls
beats.description: A Scottish explorer paddling down the Zambezi reached the thundering curtain of water and named it for his queen.

beats.title: Speke Finds Lake Victoria
beats.description: A British officer reached a vast inland lake and declared it the long-sought source of the Nile.

beats.title: British Storm Magdala
beats.description: A British-Indian army marched across the Ethiopian highlands to free captives held by the emperor, who took his own life.

beats.title: Stanley Finds Livingstone
beats.description: A newspaper reporter tracked the missing missionary to a lakeside town and greeted him with a famous line.

beats.title: Zulu War and Isandlwana
beats.description: British forces invaded Zululand and lost a whole column to the Zulu army before finally defeating the kingdom.

beats.title: Britain Occupies Egypt
beats.description: After shelling Alexandria, a British army defeated Egyptian nationalists at Tel el-Kebir and took control of the country.

beats.title: Berlin Conference Carves Up Africa
beats.description: European powers and the United States agreed rules for claiming African territory, with no African ruler in the room.
beats.note: Conference ran from late 1884; the General Act was signed in 1885.

beats.title: Ethiopia Crushes Italy at Adwa
beats.description: An Italian colonial army was routed by the forces of the Ethiopian emperor, securing the country's independence.

beats.title: Fashoda Crisis
beats.description: A small French expedition reached a fort on the upper Nile and faced down a British army, nearly sparking a war.

beats.title: Boer War Begins
beats.description: Two Afrikaner republics went to war with the British empire over gold, rights and control of southern Africa.

beats.title: Italy Invades Libya
beats.description: Italian troops landed at Tripoli and other ports, seizing North African provinces from the Ottoman Empire.

beats.title: Treaty of Fez Makes Morocco French
beats.description: A treaty signed at Fez handed the sultan's foreign affairs to France, with a zone in the north left to Spain.

beats.title: Rif Fighters Rout Spain at Annual
beats.description: Berber tribesmen under a local leader overran a Spanish army in northern Morocco in one of colonial Europe's worst defeats.

beats.title: Italy Invades Ethiopia
beats.description: Mussolini's army crossed from Eritrea, using bombers and poison gas against an emperor's poorly armed forces.
